title: The pre-commit hook runs only lint-staged
context: The repository has no hooks at all: lint, typecheck, test and check:workflow run only in CI and in the verify gates. The industry pattern is narrow: a pre-commit hook formats and lints staged files and nothing else, because a slow hook is a hook developers bypass. Agent worktrees were expected to escape hooks entirely, but testing showed husky writes a relative core.hooksPath into the shared .git/config that every worktree resolves against its own root; the generated .husky/_ directory is gitignored and recreated by pnpm install, which CONTRIBUTING.md already requires in each worktree. So hooks do reach agent worktrees, and the remaining bypasses are a worktree with no install, HUSKY=0, --no-verify, and commits created through the GitHub API.
decision: husky installs two hooks. pre-commit runs lint-staged only, which runs eslint --fix and prettier over staged files. commit-msg runs commitlint. Typechecking and tests stay out of both, because pnpm verify, pnpm verify:all and the CI static job already own them. CI re-runs commitlint over the pull request range so the four bypasses do not become holes.

alternatives.option: Run typecheck or the test suite in pre-commit
alternatives.reason: It makes every commit slow enough that --no-verify becomes routine, and the same checks already gate the branch twice.

alternatives.option: Rely on CI alone and install no hooks
alternatives.reason: The feedback arrives after the commit exists, which is what forced the rebase rewrite during two-gate-workflow; hooks do reach agent worktrees, so they are worth installing.

consequences: A worktree created but never installed silently runs no hooks; CI is the backstop.
The CI install sets HUSKY=0 so the prepare script does not run there.
revisitTriggers: Commits keep arriving in CI that the hooks would have caught, meaning worktrees are skipping installation.
